editorial:
If you want a superhero movie that never takes itself seriously, this one delivers. Ryan Reynolds returns as the masked mercenary who talks to the camera, breaks the fourth wall, and turns every fight into a joke. This time he tries to protect a troubled teen mutant from Cable, a tough soldier from the future who wants the kid dead. The story moves fast, mixing big action with silly humor and surprising heart. You get wild stunts, sharp one-liners, and a team-up that feels like a messy family road trip. It is loud, rude, and packed with cameos, but it also gives Deadpool a real reason to care about someone else.

The action is slick, the jokes land often, and the cast keeps the energy high. Some gags repeat and a few scenes feel crowded, but the movie rarely slows down. If you like superhero stories with adult humor, you will have a great time. Watch it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final act, Deadpool and Cable team up to save the boy from becoming a killer. Cable uses his last time-travel charge to stop the boy's first murder, then stays in the present. Deadpool sacrifices himself to save the boy, but Cable later uses a device to bring him back. The movie ends with Deadpool alive, joking with his friends, and teasing more adventures.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves superhero comedies with adult humor.
